f-P25b9: Kids also need transferable skills and education, relationships with people outside the community, access to their own records and documents, and at least one plausible next step outside the community (school, an apprenticeship, work, family, another community). It would be great if the community could also provide resources to smooth the transition, like temporary housing, travel expenses, tools or a little money, but even if it can't, it can at least not make things worse by punishing people for leaving, or by holding back knowledge or records a young adult would need to function outside the community. No upbringing can provide perfect freedom, and the point isn't to erase path dependence. It's to not turn belonging into a trap.
